newsitem.title: UK: PR firm Burson-Marsteller '96 revenues rise 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: PR firm Burson-Marsteller '96 revenues rise 12 pct.

text.p: Burson-Marsteller, the public relations and consulting firm owned by the Young & Rubicam advertising agency, on Thursday said its 1996 revenues rose about 12 percent to $261 million.

Revenues in Europe climbed 15 percent to $79 million. The Americas posted nine percent growth in revenues, the strongest growth for the region in five years, rising to $120 million from $110 million. The region includes the U.S., Canada and Latin America.

"Our successful European performance can be attributed to the long-term partnership with clients and the major investment we have made," Ferdinand de Bakker, European president and chief executive officer, said in a statement. Burson-Marsteller in 1996 invested $10 million in training, and over the last five years it has invested $35 million in technology.
"Most of our operations in Europe performed well in 1996, and they are poised for even stronger performance under the new client/practice structure," de Bakker said.
Tom Bell, president and chief executive officer of Burson-Marsteller worldwide, said U.S. operations performed well in the third and fourth quarters. "We see momentum continuing into 1997," he said.
Revenues for Asia in 1996 totalled $36 million, with China revenues rising 54 percent.

"Without the one-time effects of merging our operations in Korea and selling our format design and creative services business in Hong Kong, Asia-Pacific would have shown growth of 11 percent for the year," Bell said.
